sections.h2: The law behind South Carolina rentals
sections.html:
The Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Chapter 40 of Title 27 of the state code, covers most residential rentals. It sets what a lease must say, what the landlord must repair, how deposits work and how a tenancy ends.

Section 27-40-20 says the Act is to be liberally construed to promote its purposes, and 27-40-60 lets a good-faith dispute be settled by agreement. If you own a rental and plan to sell, the Act answers one practical question: what do I still owe this tenant after closing?

Every landlord owes the tenant a written statement, given by the start of the tenancy, naming an owner or an agent with authority to act for the owner, with an address (27-40-420). The repair duty is broad. Section 27-40-440 requires the landlord to make repairs and do whatever is reasonably necessary to keep the premises fit and habitable.

  • The disclosure stays current and can be enforced against a successor landlord, owner or manager (27-40-420(b)).
  • Habitability covers code compliance, running water, reasonable hot water and heat, and working electrical, plumbing and heating.
  • A tenant facing a material breach by the landlord can end the lease after written notice if it is not fixed within 14 days (27-40-610).

A buyer who takes over a tenant also takes over the repair duty, and pending complaints tend to come up in negotiations. If the house needs work, expect that conversation.

When the tenancy ends, the landlord returns the deposit minus amounts kept for rent and damages and sends an itemized written notice. The clock is thirty days, counted from the latest of three events: the tenancy ending, possession handed back, and the tenant's demand (27-40-410(a)).

A landlord who misses that step can face recovery of three times the wrongfully withheld amount plus attorney's fees. The definitions in 27-40-210 set no cap on the deposit amount.

When a rental changes hands, 27-40-410(e) and 27-40-450 decide who holds the money. Whoever holds the landlord's interest at termination is bound by the deposit rules. A good-faith seller is released once the tenant has written notice, yet still answers for the deposit until it moves to the buyer and the tenant is told. Put the deposit transfer on the closing checklist in writing.

The landlord needs 24 hours notice before entering, at reasonable times, except in an emergency (27-40-530(c)). Scheduled periodic services may happen between 9:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., and tenant-requested services between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m., with an announcement beforehand.

Retaliation is prohibited. If a tenant complains to a code enforcement agency or to the landlord, the landlord may not respond by pushing rent above fair market value, cutting essential services or filing for possession. A tenant harmed by retaliation can recover up to three months rent or treble damages (27-40-910). To use the defense against a rule to vacate, the tenant must write to the landlord within ten days of service.

Landlord or tenant may close out a month-to-month tenancy by giving thirty days or more in writing, and a weekly tenancy takes seven (27-40-770). A fixed-term lease generally runs to its end date unless a breach lets one side terminate earlier.

  • Unpaid rent: if the tenant has not paid within five days of the due date after written notice, the landlord may terminate (27-40-710(B)).
  • Other breach: termination comes no sooner than 14 days after receipt of notice if the tenant does not remedy it (27-40-710(A)).
  • Abandonment: an unexplained absence for 15 days after a rent default may be treated as abandonment (27-40-730).

Lockouts and utility shutoffs are not a legal way to recover possession (27-40-760). The route is court, and the magistrate steps are in Chapter 37 of the same title.

sections.h2: What happens to the lease when you sell
sections.html:
The statutes hand you notice and deposit duties, and they do not by themselves end the tenancy. Whether a buyer takes subject to the lease depends on the lease terms and the buyer's deal, so have an attorney review the specifics.

Before any buyer call, pull together:

  • The signed lease with every addendum, plus the current rent ledger.
  • How much the deposit is and where the money sits.
  • A record of repair requests and your responses, since habitability disputes carry over in practice.
  • Written notice to the tenant of the new owner and contact details, as 27-40-420 and 27-40-450 contemplate.

If the tenant is behind or the house is in poor shape, some owners sell as-is for cash and let the buyer decide what to do about the tenancy. Weigh that against selling vacant.

sections.h2: Costs a rental owner should expect at sale
sections.html:
Plan for property tax proration and a deed recording fee. Real estate taxes fall due between September 30 and January 15. After that the penalty is 3 percent, with 7 percent added after February 2 and 5 percent after March 17 (12-45-70 and 12-45-180).

Recording costs $1.85 for every $500 of value ($1.30 state, $0.55 county), and the grantor is normally the one who pays (12-24-10 and 12-24-20). A rented house is assessed at 6 percent as other real property. An owner-occupied legal residence gets 4 percent only if it is not rented for more than 72 days in a calendar year (12-43-220).

sections.h2: Rent terms and leases with no end date
sections.html:
Rent is payable at the start of each month, or at the start of any term of one month or less, and it can be apportioned day to day unless the parties agree otherwise. With no fixed term, the tenancy is month to month (27-40-310).

Day-to-day proration helps at a closing, since rent for the part of a month after the sale date can be divided on the settlement statement. A landlord also cannot enforce an unperfected contractual lien on a tenant's household goods (27-40-740).

sections.h2: Health and safety violations by a tenant
sections.html:
After 14 days written notice, or sooner in an emergency, the landlord may enter and do the work or terminate the lease if the tenant fails to comply (27-40-720). A tenant can raise maintenance defenses and counterclaims in a possession or rent case under 27-40-640, though some defenses are waived if the landlord lacked notice 14 days before rent was due.

Property worth $500 or less left behind after abandonment may be disposed of under 27-40-730, and the landlord is liable above that figure only if grossly negligent. Hold on to dated photographs. A buyer's lender or inspector may want to see them.

faqs.q: How long does a landlord have to return a deposit in South Carolina?
faqs.a: Thirty days after the tenancy ends and possession is delivered, or after the tenant demands it, whichever is later. A landlord who fails to send the itemized notice and money can owe three times the amount wrongfully withheld plus attorney's fees (27-40-410).

faqs.q: Is there a cap on security deposits?
faqs.a: The Act's definitions in 27-40-210 set no cap or amount limit. Check your lease for the agreed amount.

faqs.q: Can a landlord enter without notice?
faqs.a: Only in an emergency. Otherwise 24 hours notice and reasonable times apply under 27-40-530.

faqs.q: Can a tenant withhold rent for repairs?
faqs.a: Section 27-40-640 does not create a general right to withhold rent. It lets a tenant raise defenses and counterclaims in a possession or rent action, and some maintenance defenses are waived if the landlord lacked timely notice.

faqs.q: What if a landlord retaliates after a complaint?
faqs.a: Retaliation is barred, and a landlord can owe up to three months rent or treble actual damages plus fees under 27-40-910. The tenant must give written notice of the defense within ten days after service of a rule to vacate.
